# Records captured verbatim from a running Linux 6.6 kernel's /dev/kmsg on the
# build host, 2026-08-24. NOT hand-composed: `AGENTS.md` §4 — "a vector captured
# from real hardware is worth more than a hand-composed one, and the difference
# must be visible in the file."
#
# Selected rather than edited. Lines carrying anything host-specific — the
# kernel's build identifier, a command line, a machine-id inside a path — were
# DROPPED rather than rewritten (`AGENTS.md` §8.3), so every line below is
# exactly what the kernel wrote. These `#` lines are not part of the capture and
# the reader skips them; a real /dev/kmsg has no comments.
#
# What the selection covers:
#
#   7,22,...     debug     facility 0 (kernel), a low priority
#   6,301,...    info      facility 0, and the only record here with the
#                          continuation lines a device message carries
#   4,157,...    warning   facility 0
#   3,224,...    error     facility 0 — the class ADR-004 §8 expects to
#                          dominate Stage 2 diagnosis
#   14,404,...   info      facility 1, so `prifac >> 3` is exercised and a
#                          reader that took the whole number as a priority
#                          fails here
#   46,448,...   info      facility 5, likewise, and from userspace rather
#                          than from the kernel
#
# What it does NOT cover, and is therefore tested from the specification with
# that said out loud: priorities 0, 1 and 2 (emerg, alert, crit). A healthy
# machine does not produce them, which is the point of them.

4,157,54256,-;Hyper-V: Disabling IBT because of Hyper-V bug
3,224,83932,-;PCI: Fatal: No config space access function found
14,404,222986,-;WSL (1 - ): WSL version 2.7.3.0
46,448,1158481,-;systemd-journald[42]: Collecting audit messages is enabled.
6,301,124628,-;pci_bus 5582:00: root bus resource [mem 0x9ffe00000-0x9ffe02fff window]
